sections: Auditing a new machine with the four laws
A packaging cell across the three machine classes

blocks.md: This lesson follows **Generalizing to Unfamiliar Systems** in *Engineering Physical AI* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Engineering Physical AI, § Generalizing to Unfamiliar Systems
blocks.md: An automated packaging cell that shuttles containers, seats closure tabs, and repeats high-rate cycles across a full shift can ram a closing gate, crush a carton wall, or bake its motor windings if its learned proposers outrun its physical limits. Building it requires the same pairing as the warehouse machine: a capable learned proposer with an execution pipeline whose runtime authority respects kinematic reach, contact force, and thermal buildup in the drive motors. The four bedrock laws trace one chain through such a machine.

questions.q: The section **Generalizing to Unfamiliar Systems** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A premise no onboard sensor reports is not the envelope's monitored unknown, so it is bound to a standing restriction, an accountable owner, and a predeclared closure test, chosen among responses (probe, restrict, add sensing, accept by judgment) by the claim each can support.

A shield's per-command guarantee becomes a hazard-rate claim only conditionally, lambda_sys <= lambda_h(1 - c) + lambda_cc, and observed fleet rates already include the shield, so multiplying them by an interception factor double-counts.

The method transfers to an unfamiliar machine as four ordered questions (what the task cannot undo and which measured bound excludes it, whether closed-loop evidence covers the enforced envelope, which independent path admits each proposal, and what evidence bounds the authority granted), not as the warehouse machine's numbers.

When two states that need different responses produce identical observations until the action deadline, no model on that channel can separate them, and the latest useful observation is set by braking distance over speed.
